requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).

hunches.claim: The new metadata-type guard exits for every referenced generic type, including closed generic classes. Those classes previously went through CollectGeneric and received a formatter in the consuming compilation; now only Cmd gets generated code and Lib.Item<int> has no formatter. This violates the acceptance criterion that closed generic classes keep working as before and can break their AOT serialization.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.MetadataGenericClassCompatibilityTests.ClosedGenericClassFromReferencedAssembly_KeepsGeneratedFormatter. It compiles a metadata Lib.Item<T> class reference, runs the generator on the consuming app, and requires a generated implementation of IMessagePackFormatter<Lib.Item<int>>. It passes on base and fails on head because the unconditional OriginalDefinition.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty guard skips collection.

hunches.claim: MsgPack005 is silently dropped for a source-declared positional record property with `[property: Key(null)]`. Such a property's declaration syntax is a `ParameterSyntax`, not a `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`, so `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` returns null. The resulting diagnostic has `Location.None`, and `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` discards it even though the offending member belongs to the current source compilation.

receipt_plan.detail: Run MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer over `[MessagePackObject] public partial record MyRecord([property: Key(null)] string Value);` and assert that its analyzer diagnostics include MsgPack005. On head, the property helper returns null and the new location filter suppresses the diagnostic.

hunches.claim: The added tests only exercise valid usage declarations and expect zero diagnostics, so they provide no positive control that the new diagnostic filter still reports legitimate diagnostics from the usage compilation. An implementation that discards every diagnostic would satisfy all three added tests.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1451 delete-statement: report(diagnostic); -> deleted; expected to survive the added tests because none declares an invalid source type or expects a diagnostic, so they cannot distinguish correct filtering from suppressing every diagnostic.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L8] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: Metadata-only generic types now receive no analysis or formatter from the consuming compilation, matching the established policy that the defining assembly owns validation and formatting of its types; this is deliberate rather than a defect.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] Types from referenced assemblies are deliberately not analysed and receive no formatter from the compiling assembly; the defining assembly owns validation and formatting, so missing diagnostics or formatters for them are not defects.
